data.narrative:
Ample, a Series C Climate & Energy company founded by Khaled Hassounah and John De Souza, has raised $720.2M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a peer set of three same-sector, same-stage comparables—KoBold Metals ($3.0B), Electric Hydrogen ($1.0B), and Amogy ($700M)—supplemented by a broader universe of eight private and one public company operating in climate tech infrastructure.

Two triangulation methods are applicable. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.7x step-up multiplier to the $720M total capital raised as a proxy baseline, yielding $1.2B. Peer-median valuation across the three direct comparables produces $1.0B, with a range spanning $700M to $3.0B. The wide spread reflects divergence in business model maturity and capital intensity within the cohort.

Synthesizing both methods produces a median implied valuation of $1.1B, with a defensible range of $850M to $1.4B. The stage-progression and peer-median methods converge relatively closely, strengthening confidence in the midpoint. Key uncertainties include the comparables' capital efficiency trajectories and revenue visibility, both of which drive valuation variance in climate-tech Series C rounds. The peer range notably reflects KoBold's outlier valuation; excluding it tightens the spread materially.
